subject: Archival band pricing & dashboard seat split — packaging question
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@olivehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Observability add-ons — retention, tracing, dashboards (RFP attached)

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We're moving this RFP through procurement and there's one open area we need clearer pricing on: archival/retention tiers for traces and spans, and how advanced dashboards are licensed alongside seat vs. slab retention. The RFP assumes a simple per-GB archival fee + dashboard seats, but that doesn't capture our bursty trace ingestion during Sync windows.

Questions we have: 
- Do you support a month-to-month slab for archival (e.g., 0-2TB, 2-10TB, 10TB+)?
- If we commit to a 12-mo archival volume, do you provide crediting for unused retention?
- Can dashboards be split off as a per-seat add-on so we only pay for 12 analysts, while retention is metered across services?

I attached the RFP and a sample of our recent ingestion profile. Can you propose 2–3 packaging options (pilot, committed, enterprise) and a sample invoice for each?

We're on a procurement review next week (11/12) and would prefer to lock in a pilot path if the economics look reasonable.

Regards,
Ellie Park
Head of Data Platforms
OliveHealth

Attachments: RFP_olivehealth_obs.pdf
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention, tracing, dashboards (RFP attached)

Hi Ellie — thanks for the RFP and the ingestion profile, that's very helpful. I sketched three packaging approaches and attached a pricing grid for clarity. High level: 

1) Metered (Pay-as-you-go) 
- Archival: $0.02/GB-month for first 2TB, $0.015/GB-month for 2-10TB, $0.01/GB-month beyond that.
- Dashboards: per-seat monthly at $125/seat.
- Pros: no commit, aligns with bursty ingestion.
- Cons: higher unit cost at scale, less predictability.

2) Slab Commit (12-month) 
- Commit to a slab (e.g., 10TB/month) at a blended rate 20% below metered. Unused capacity can be converted into a one-time credit toward dashboards or training, up to 30% of the committed amount per quarter.
- Dashboards: discounted bundle rate if seat commitment > 20 seats.

3) Hybrid Pilot (90-day) + Enterprise Rollout 
- 90-day pilot with fixed retention cap (e.g., 3TB) at a pilot rate and up to one-time onboarding credit.
- On conversion to enterprise, pilot fees can roll into the commitment with a pro-rated credit.

Notes and tradeoffs: 
- For heavy burst windows, KV prefix caching will reduce archival amplification — we can show an expected effective rate reduction after sampling your 3-week sync.
- Tracing: sampling tiers (1%, 10%, 100%) change costs non-linearly; we recommend a 10% sample for analytics + 100% for a rolling 72-hour debug window.

I've attached pricing_grid_v1.xlsx and a short draft SOW to show pilot deliverables. If it helps I can put together a sample invoice per option; Ben and Kim, can you weigh in on concession levers (credits, SLAs, seat discounts)?

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: observability-pricing-grid.xlsx, SOW-draft-olivehealth.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention, tracing, dashboards (RFP attached)

Connor / Kim — quick thoughts: 

- Offer a 12-month commit option with a tiered crediting rule: unused committed GBs can be banked for up to two quarters and then either converted to a dashboard credit or refunded at 50% of list. That gives procurement something tangible.
- For the pilot, we can give a one-time 30% onboarding credit toward the first invoice if they sign an LOI within 30 days.
- SLA: provide a 99.9% ingestion uptime for dedicated ingestion windows; higher SLAs tied to Dedicated capacity only.

Kim, please create a packaging snippet that separates dashboards as "visualization seats" and makes it easy to swap into a seat-only renewal clause. Also flag any legal SOW gotchas (retention SLAs, data residency).

Ben
Senior Director, Sales

From: Ellie Park <ellie@olivehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention, tracing, dashboards (RFP attached)

Connor — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need.

On a couple of points: 
- Procurement prefers a 12-month commit but needs a clearer unused-credit conversion formula; the bank-for-quarters approach sounds reasonable — can you show sample math for 10TB commit with 2TB unused in Q2?
- The pilot onboarding credit is attractive, but legal needs the SOW language tightened around data deletion timelines and export rights.
- Dashboard seat split is a must for my analysts; we're comfortable with 12 seats initially. Can you produce three sample invoices (metered, slab-commit, hybrid pilot) and include the pro-forma where the pilot credit rolls forward? Procurement review is on 11/12 — if you can send invoices + the sample credit math by EOD 11/10 we'll include it in the packet.

I'll be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow 11/10 10:00-10:30am PT if that helps speed decisions.

Best,
Ellie
